incidents.title: Harbourside Market stabbing, Port Ellery
incidents.summary: Two people injured, one seriously, at Harbourside Market at about 13:50. A man was arrested at the scene.

incidents.title: Missing child found safe, Brennford
incidents.summary: A 9-year-old reported missing at 12:10 was found safe and well at a relative's home at 13:05.

incidents.title: March and counter-protest, Kingsbridge
incidents.summary: A march of about 6,000 and a counter-protest of about 800 are planned for Saturday afternoon.

incidents.title: River Teg flood warning, Aberteg
incidents.summary: Severe flood warning for the lower Teg valley. Rest centre open at Ysgol Aberteg (fictional).

narratives.title: False suspect identity: 'man from the Harbourside hotel'
narratives.claim: The attacker is an asylum seeker living at the Harbourside hotel.
narratives.truth: The arrested man is a 34-year-old British man from Port Ellery (verified by the SIO).

narratives.title: Cover-up: 'police are hiding who did it'
narratives.claim: Police silence proves they are covering up the attacker's identity.
narratives.truth: Proceedings are active; police publish verified facts as they are confirmed.

narratives.title: Recycled footage: 2019 disorder video posted as 'Port Ellery tonight'
narratives.claim: Video shows rioting in Port Ellery this afternoon.
narratives.truth: The clip is from an unrelated 2019 event in another country (fictional reverse-search match).

narratives.title: Fake 'police curfew notice' on a spoof force website
narratives.claim: Northmoor Police has imposed a 6pm curfew on all residents.
narratives.truth: No curfew exists. The notice is on a spoof domain with indicators matching a state-linked network.

narratives.title: Call to gather at the Harbourside hotel on Saturday night
narratives.claim: Posts urge people to 'take back the harbour' at the hotel at 19:00, some with threats.
narratives.truth: A small share of posts contain threats and may be illegal content for referral.

narratives.title: AI-generated image of an officer kneeling on a child
narratives.claim: Photo shows a Kingsbridge officer kneeling on a child at the march.
narratives.truth: The image carries generation artefacts and matches no event (fictional forensic check).

narratives.title: 'Two-tier policing' at the Kingsbridge march
narratives.claim: Police treat one side of the march more leniently than the other.
narratives.truth: Contested opinion. Lawful speech: monitor the narrative only; respond with facts about the policing plan.

narratives.title: 'Second child taken' rumour in Brennford
narratives.claim: A second child has been abducted from the same park.
narratives.truth: No second child is missing. The first child was found safe at 13:05.

narratives.title: Flood hoax: 'dam about to fail, evacuate now' (Welsh and English)
narratives.claim: Llyn Teg dam is failing and everyone must leave immediately.
narratives.truth: The dam is sound (fictional reservoir operator). Follow the official flood warning only.

narratives.title: Jury speculation in the Halden Street trial
narratives.claim: Posts name the 16-year-old defendant and claim he has previous convictions.
narratives.truth: Reporting restrictions apply. Refer contempt breaches; police comms must not repeat details.

scenarios.title: Golden Hour: Harbourside Market stabbing
scenarios.goal: Shrink time to truth on a false suspect identity, with every release legally checked and signed off.

steps.do: Declare the critical incident and open the Golden Hour cell
Log the first facts: time, place, two injured, one man arrested
Verify the facts in the fact log
Draft a holding statement and run it through Safe to Say
Legal review of the holding statement
SIO approves the statement
Gold signs off; press officer publishes
Radar alert on NAR-01 (false identity). Triage it and link it to the incident
Record a disclosure decision on nationality (interim ethnicity and nationality guidance)
Home Office responds to the request to confirm immigration status
Draft a national line on speculation about the suspect
Approve and cascade the national line to all forces
Forces acknowledge the line (Severnvale, Dyfed-Glas with Welsh version, Kingsbridge)
Ethics panel reviews the decision trail: every decision has a named person and a reason

scenarios.title: Spoof curfew notice with state-linked indicators
scenarios.goal: Debunk a spoof notice fast, pass indicators to CTP and government, and never attribute publicly.

steps.do: Triage NAR-04 and hand state-linked indicators to CTP and government
CTP liaison accepts the handover
Draft a rebuttal. Safe to Say blocks any public attribution to a state actor
Publish the corrected rebuttal (no attribution, points to official channels as in LN-002)

scenarios.title: Mobilisation and threats: platform referral
scenarios.goal: Refer possible illegal content to the platform and CTIRU, and track response times as evidence.

steps.do: SIB analyst assesses community tension for Port Ellery from NAR-05
Log a referral of the threatening post to the platform
Record the platform's response and time taken

scenarios.title: Two-tier narrative at a protest (lawful opinion)
scenarios.goal: Respond with facts about the policing plan without treating lawful opinion as a threat or profiling commentators.

steps.do: Try to add the commentator account behind NAR-07 to a watchlist: Line of Blue refuses (Tier D)
Draft a policing plan explainer and pass the impartiality checks

scenarios.title: Bilingual flood hoax (civil emergency)
scenarios.goal: Counter a hoax in Welsh and English under the warning and informing duty.

steps.do: Draft a bilingual rebuttal. Safe to Say flags a missing Welsh version until one is added

scenarios.title: Youth trial and complainant anonymity (hard blocks)
scenarios.goal: Prove that drafts naming a child defendant or identifying a complainant cannot be released.

steps.do: Draft about the Halden Street trial that names the defendant: hard block
Draft that mentions Rivermead Close and the complainant's age: hard block

scenarios.title: Get ahead: pre-bunk the spoof curfew before it appears
scenarios.goal: Use the rumour forecast and the L.O.B Agent to publish a signed-off pre-bunk before the first spoof notice is posted.

steps.do: Declare the critical incident. The rumour forecast appears in the cell
Ask the L.O.B Agent for a get-ahead plan, with the guidance it rests on
Send the spoof-notice pre-bunk from the forecast to Safe to Say and submit it
Legal review of the pre-bunk
SIO approves the pre-bunk
Gold signs off the pre-bunk
Publish the pre-bunk
On the National picture, confirm the police line was out before the first spoof notice

knowledge.title: Contempt of Court Act 1981
knowledge.summary: Strict liability rule (ss.1-2): a publication that creates a substantial risk of serious prejudice to active proceedings is contempt, whatever the intent. Proceedings are active from arrest or warrant. s.4(2) postponement orders and s.11 orders restrict reporting.
knowledge.comms: Once a suspect is arrested, avoid comment on guilt, motive, character or previous convictions. Stick to verified facts: what happened, where, when, and that a person is in custody.

knowledge.title: Contempt of court report, part 1 (18 Nov 2025)
knowledge.summary: Recommends proceedings become active at charge rather than arrest, and that a suspect's name, age, nationality, ethnicity, religion and immigration status would generally not create a substantial risk of prejudice. Government has not yet legislated; part 2 due 2026.
knowledge.comms: Not yet law. Line of Blue keeps the active-proceedings trigger configurable so the rules can change the day the law does.

knowledge.title: Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 1992
knowledge.summary: Complainants of sexual offences have lifelong anonymity. Nothing likely to identify them may be published.
knowledge.comms: Hard block: no names, ages, streets, workplaces or other details that could identify a complainant, even in combination.

knowledge.title: Children and Young Persons Act 1933 s.49 and YJCEA 1999 s.45
knowledge.summary: Automatic reporting restrictions for children in youth court, and discretionary restrictions for under-18s in adult courts. The Southport defendant was 17.
knowledge.comms: Do not name or describe a child defendant or witness unless the court lifts restrictions.

knowledge.title: Media and communications APP (replaces Media relations APP; consulted 5 Nov 2025 to 4 Jan 2026)
knowledge.summary: Six principles: open justice, privacy, legitimacy, accurate and lawful, timely and consistent, inclusive and impartial. Expects forces to tackle mis/disinformation that affects public safety or justice, and to keep better records. Suspects are not normally named before charge.
knowledge.comms: Fill the information void with verified facts quickly, record each disclosure decision and its reasons, and challenge false narratives that threaten safety or justice.

knowledge.owner: College of Policing and NPCC (with CPS and Home Office)
knowledge.title: Interim guidance on suspect ethnicity and nationality (Aug 2025)
knowledge.summary: In high-profile cases where misinformation is causing tension, forces should consider confirming a suspect's ethnicity and nationality. Only the Home Office confirms immigration status. Decisions and reasons should be recorded.
knowledge.comms: When a false identity claim is spreading on a live case, put a disclosure decision to Gold quickly; request Home Office confirmation before saying anything about immigration status.

knowledge.owner: NPCC, College, CPS, Society of Editors, CRA, MLA
knowledge.title: Policing and Media Charter (17 Mar 2026)
knowledge.summary: Forces publish press office contact numbers, give direct updates to accredited media, and appoint a journalist safety liaison officer in every force.
knowledge.comms: Brief accredited media directly and early; they carry the verified line further and faster than police channels alone.

knowledge.title: CPS-police Media Protocol
knowledge.summary: Sets what prosecution material can be released and when, before and after charge and at trial.
knowledge.comms: Check the protocol before releasing images, footage or case detail after charge.

knowledge.title: Human Rights Act 1998 Art 8 and Sir Cliff Richard v BBC [2018]
knowledge.summary: A suspect under investigation normally has a reasonable expectation of privacy. Interference must be lawful, necessary and proportionate.
knowledge.comms: Do not identify an uncharged suspect without a recorded, proportionate reason.

knowledge.title: Defamation Act 2013
knowledge.summary: Statements and reposts can be defamatory; repeating an allegation can carry liability.
knowledge.comms: Describe a false claim rather than reposting it or linking to its source.

knowledge.title: Pre-election period guidance
knowledge.summary: During general, devolved, local, mayoral and PCC election periods, avoid any activity that could be seen as favouring a party or candidate. PCC elections end in May 2028.
knowledge.comms: In a pre-election period, talk about the policing plan and facts, never parties, candidates or politically loaded labels.

knowledge.title: Code of Ethics (2024), Standards of Professional Behaviour, Police Regulations 2003 Sch.1
knowledge.summary: Police must act with impartiality and must not take part in politics or appear partisan.
knowledge.comms: Answer 'two-tier policing' claims with facts about how both sides are policed; never mock or label either side.

knowledge.title: Equality Act 2010 s.149 (public sector equality duty)
knowledge.summary: Due regard to eliminating discrimination, advancing equality and fostering good relations.
knowledge.comms: Consider community impact of every line during tension; involve independent advisory groups early.

knowledge.title: Welsh Language (Wales) Measure 2011 and Welsh Language Standards
knowledge.summary: Welsh forces must communicate bilingually and treat Welsh no less favourably than English.
knowledge.comms: Publish Welsh and English together in Wales; a hoax in Welsh needs a rebuttal in Welsh.

knowledge.title: Civil Contingencies Act 2004 (warning and informing duty)
knowledge.summary: Police are Category 1 responders with a legal duty to warn and inform the public in emergencies.
knowledge.comms: In a civil emergency, one joined-up public message with partners, repeated on every channel.

knowledge.title: JESIP joint doctrine
knowledge.summary: Shared multi-agency situational awareness and joint decision-making, including public messaging.
knowledge.comms: Agree the public line with fire, ambulance, council and NHS so the public hears one story.

knowledge.title: RIPA 2000 Part II and Covert Surveillance Code of Practice (2018) paras 3.10-3.17
knowledge.summary: Viewing public posts is usually fine. Systematically collecting and recording information about a particular person or group may be directed surveillance needing authorisation. Broad thematic research usually does not.
knowledge.comms: Monitor narratives and topics, not people. Any watchlist of individuals needs a recorded RIPA authorisation through intelligence channels.

knowledge.title: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 Part 3 (as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025)
knowledge.summary: Lawful basis, purpose limitation, minimisation, retention limits and a DPIA. Politics, religion and ethnicity are special category data.
knowledge.comms: Aggregate and pseudonymise by default; keep decision records, not scraped personal data.

knowledge.title: Human Rights Act 1998 Art 10 and 11
knowledge.summary: Expression, including views that offend, shock or disturb, and lawful assembly are protected.
knowledge.comms: Never treat lawful but unwelcome opinion as a threat. Respond with facts, not action against speakers.

knowledge.title: Online Safety Act 2023
knowledge.summary: Platform duties regulated by Ofcom; offences including false communications (s.179) and threatening communications (s.181).
knowledge.comms: Police are not the regulator. Refer illegal content to platforms or Ofcom and log the response time.

knowledge.title: Terrorism Act 2000 (proscription, ss.12-13) and CTIRU referrals
knowledge.summary: Supporting or displaying support for a proscribed group is an offence. Terrorist content goes to CTIRU.
knowledge.comms: Route terrorist content to CTIRU, not to a comms response.

knowledge.title: National Security Act 2023 and Foreign Influence Registration Scheme (live 1 Jul 2025)
knowledge.summary: Foreign interference is an offence and a national security matter. Attribution is decided by government, not by police communications.
knowledge.comms: Debunk the content, pass indicators to CTP and government, never name a state in public lines.

knowledge.title: Government response on non-crime hate incidents (31 Mar 2026)
knowledge.summary: Non-crime hate incidents were scrapped; police should not record lawful speech against people.
knowledge.comms: Do not log lawful but offensive posts as incidents about the people who wrote them.

knowledge.title: RESIST counter-disinformation toolkit and evaluation framework
knowledge.summary: Government standard to Recognise, Early warning, Situational insight, Impact analysis, Strategic communication and Track disinformation. Endorses pre-bunking and measuring outcomes.
knowledge.comms: Pre-bunk likely falsehoods before they spread, choose the response by impact, and measure whether it worked.

knowledge.title: Police response to the public disorder in July and August 2024 (Tranche 2)
knowledge.summary: Police 'have not kept pace' with online communications. 'Policing cannot be passive when public safety is at risk': forces must fill the information void and challenge false narratives. 1,804 arrests and 1,071 charged by 22 Jan 2025. Disorder mostly driven by disaffected individuals and online influencers, not one organised group.
knowledge.comms: Speed matters most. Narrative-first monitoring catches what watchlists miss.

knowledge.title: Policing took action, now others must step up (May 2025)
knowledge.summary: NPCC is developing misinformation monitoring built on the social listening used in 2024, wants a proactive communications model, and is working more closely with the Cabinet Office. Police should not regulate social media.
knowledge.comms: The stated national requirement Line of Blue answers: a proactive, coordinated comms model.

knowledge.title: From local to national: a new model for policing (Jan 2026)
knowledge.summary: A National Police Service absorbs NPCC coordination, the College and the Police Digital Service and provides 'a single national voice for communicating with the public'. Trust fell from 80% (2015/16) to 71% (2024/25). PCCs end in May 2028.
knowledge.comms: One national voice, consistent local delivery: national lines cascade, forces localise.

knowledge.title: From rumours to riots (31 Jul 2024)
knowledge.summary: The false Southport name was published by a small site and amplified by large accounts within hours. No foreign state role was found.
knowledge.comms: False identity claims appear within the first hour of a critical incident; prepare for them at declaration.

knowledge.title: UK sanctions on Social Design Agency, Structura and ANO Dialog (28 Oct 2024)
knowledge.summary: Sanctioned for the Doppelganger network: at least 120 sites imitating real news and government pages, and attempts to incite protest in about six European countries.
knowledge.comms: Spoof official notices are a known tactic. Pre-bunk them: 'we only publish notices on our own website'.

Critical incident.action: Put a nationality disclosure decision to Gold now; ask the Home Office to stand by on immigration status.

Critical incident.prebunk: We know people want to know more. We will update every hour, even when there is little new to say, and explain why some details cannot be shared yet.
Critical incident.action: Commit to an hourly update rhythm and brief accredited media directly.
